opportunity: A 64-bit value a function builds in its one return register from two 32-bit halves lost a half and the argument that fed it: `((u64)hi << 32) | lo` at gcc/clang -O0 printed `unsigned int join_lo_hi(unsigned int a0) { return a0; }`, and `((u64)(a + 1) << 32) | b` at -O2 printed `int join_hi_sum(int a0) { return a0 + 1; }` (the high half returned as the whole value).
test_name: tests/stages/kuna-returnpiece.xml (10 assertions; 9 fail on main, the control passes on both) + kuna-cli/tests/decompile_all_cli.rs a_value_built_in_one_return_register_round_trips_through_the_printed_c + kuna_returnuncomputed/tests.rs (3 new unit tests)
change_kind: strict correctness fix (no option: it only stops the return-pair repair from dropping bits the function computes into its return register)
inspiration: kuna_returnuncomputed (the (ida) uncomputed-half repair) and kuna_retinputhalf's placement test
root_cause: strip_uncomputed_return_piece (ActionOutputPrototype) took any two-input PIECE defining a RETURN's value for the RDX:RAX pair return recovery joins, and judged each half by whether its move-only source sat at the half's OWN address. `((u64)hi << 32) | lo` becomes `RAX:8 = PIECE(ESI, EDI)`, whose halves are the argument registers themselves, so both read as the caller's leftover: the RETURN was cut to EDI and ESI lost its only reader. With a computed high half and an argument low half the (true,false) arm kept the HIGH half alone. Found by tracing the RETURN input after every action apply: PIECE through markimplied, the bare low half right after outputprototype.
fix: Each half is judged against the storage it occupies in the returned value (its register of a join, from the join record; or its bytes of the one register, endian-aware); the high half of a value held in one location is never kept alone. A never-written high half at its own slot (RAX's upper half after a callee returning int; 241 firings in a 45-binary survey) is still dropped.

class_coverage.x86_64: gcc/clang -O0: join from two args, from the 3rd and 6th arg, signed, computed hi + arg lo, arg hi + computed lo, lo after waitpid(&lo); -O2: computed hi + arg lo. All fixed; join_hi_lo control unchanged.
class_coverage.other_arches: clang objects, functions changed main -> fix: AArch64 -O0 5, ARM -O0 2 / -O2 3 (incl. a copy-propagated r0:r1 pair half), MIPSel -O0 5 / -O2 6, PPC64LE -O0 2, RISC-V64 -O0 5, i386 -O0/-O2 2 each (EDX:EAX join); each now returns all 8 bytes, with every argument that feeds them, in the right half order (all little-endian).
class_coverage.big_endian_note: Separate pre-existing defect, not fixed here: a big-endian two-register return is joined with the first register as the low word (build_return_output and build_call_output_pair assume trial 0 is low), so PPC32/MIPS-BE pairs print swapped on main (clang -O2 `long long wide_mul(int,int)` -> CONCAT44(low, high)). PPC32 join_lo_hi/join_lo_sum/join_keep_lo move from one half kept (wrong) to both halves kept and printed swapped (wrong for that reason).
